supporting_observations.claim: During the alerted window, WS-RDIAZ-01 made multiple connections to 10.56.20.30:8080, the inventoried explicit proxy. The available records show generic HTTP connections to that proxy, including examples at 13:30, 13:33, 13:38, 13:42, 13:56, 14:02, and 14:07 UTC.

The supplied records do not identify the external HTTPS destinations or the originating process for those proxy connections, so they do not establish whether the traffic was the approved GradeBook Pro updater or another service.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records for the alerted-period connections are generic Zeek HTTP connection summaries to the internal proxy; they do not provide external hostnames, URLs, or HTTPS tunnel details.
The supplied alerted-period connection records do not associate the proxy traffic with a process or executable.
The evidence provided is not sufficient to verify the alert's claimed roughly five-minute cadence across the full 13:30–14:10 UTC interval.
claims_not_established: That the connections were to update.gradebookpro.com or were generated by the approved GradeBook Pro updater.
That the traffic was command-and-control, data exfiltration, or otherwise malicious.
That the traffic was benign or authorized.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy CONNECT and SSL-inspection records for WS-RDIAZ-01 during 13:20–14:20 UTC that identify destinations, timestamps, and transferred bytes.
Endpoint network telemetry or process-to-socket records for the alerted connections, including executable path, user, and command line.
GradeBook Pro updater execution and update logs for the workstation during the alerted period.
The alert's underlying flow records or detection details to validate the claimed periodicity and identify the external endpoints.
unrelated_findings: Separate triage: help-desk user tess.hart launched MSRA targeting WS-RDIAZ-01 and used raul.diaz credentials; a subsequent network logon for tess.hart on WS-RDIAZ-01 is recorded. This is outside the alerted outbound-HTTPS activity and should be checked against support authorization. (T275-00050, T275-00053, T275-00066, T275-00067)

Separate triage: WS-RDIAZ-01 shows system-process activity after the alerted window, including a Winmgmt svchost launch, msiexec access to services.exe, and a dllhost.exe write to the Common Startup Shell Folders registry value. These records alone do not establish maliciousness and do not decide this alert. (T275-00310, T275-00311, T275-00314, T275-00315)
Separate triage: WS-RDIAZ-01 made an SMB connection to DC-ORC-01 that was associated with an ANONYMOUS LOGON network logon. (T275-00304, T275-00306, T275-00307, T275-00308)
